summary: Independent bounded M3 review identified one medium unsupported-projection defect: provider-backed Crosswalk Analyst proposals bypass the new deterministic mapping provenance, confidence and family-stage caps. No additional supported medium/high issue was identified in the other inspected approval, citation, autonomy, licensing or public-measure paths.
coverage: Read root startup context, isolated AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md, M3 milestone requirements in docs/development-phase-2.md, review brief, adversarial-review skill/contract. Fresh review context contained task scope and concurrency notices rather than an author diagnosis; no delegation or Git commands used.

apps/server/src/services/proposal-validation.ts and visua.ts proposal creation/preview/approval/application: strict payload schemas, server-generated review scope, immutable check/projection/review references, runtime autonomy allowlist, HTTP approval-token enforcement in app.ts, source state revalidation and failure savepoints.

apps/server/src/services/proposal-review.ts and storage/store.ts: preview snapshots, source presentation, token inputs, transaction rollback and after-commit callback isolation; read supporting proposal-review.test.ts and proposal-validation.test.ts cases.

packages/frameworks/src/search.ts and search-citations.test.ts: exact normalized contiguous quotes, canonical chunk metadata/SHA256, duplicate identities, ambiguity, changed editions and omission of invented ellipses. Matching provenance is explicitly disclaimed as proof of the attached conclusion.

packages/core/src/crosswalk.ts, levels.ts and crosswalk-projections.test.ts: relationship direction, weak/publisher-status confidence, conflicting assessments, family-stage conversion, caps and exclusion of unknown/threat families. Traced both offline and provider-backed callers in packages/agents/src/{offline,tools,agents,claude,runtime}.ts.

packages/agents/src/{tools,mode,policies}.ts and corpus-claims.test.ts: restricted citation rejection, source-preserving evidence/task withholding, provider tool-result serialization, supported policy vocabularies and failure on unsupported mixed scope. No provider calls were made.

apps/server/src/services/trust.ts, packages/core/src/{trust,scoring}.ts, connector result titles and trust.test.ts: per-connector/configuration/check grouping over complete history, observation-time filtering, public metadata allowlist, law/disabled/private/threat framework publication, evidence evaluation time and numeric measure basis.

apps/web/src/pages/{TrustPage,SettingsPage,EvidencePage}.tsx and components/{work/EvidenceCollectionDetails,agents/Proposals}.tsx: organization-authored headline attribution, measure limitations, recorded configuration labels, provenance/assurance labels, safe autonomy choices and mapping-source review presentation.

Executed only claims-review-reproductions/provider-crosswalk.mjs with database environment variables unset and explicit SQLite :memory: service. Exit 0; provider-crosswalk-result.json records deterministic refusal versus generic provider-tool staging, exact-token human approval and resulting level. No live data, network/provider, browser, build or full-suite execution.

findings.location: packages/agents/src/agents.ts:80; packages/agents/src/tools.ts:494; apps/server/src/services/visua.ts checkProposal projection conditional (payload.projection !== undefined)
findings.mechanism: The provider-backed crosswalk-analyst is still allowed to call propose_assessment. That tool accepts any valid current level and model confidence, and always omits payload.projection. The service only recomputes mapping strength, source identity, confidence and family caps when that optional field is present. Thus a mapping-only provider proposal bypasses every new projection constraint and its review preview has no bound mapping source. The offline analyst uses proposeCrosswalkAssessment and correctly refuses the identical weak mapping, so behavior diverges by runtime mode.
findings.evidence: Synthetic in-memory reproduction, claims-review-reproductions/provider-crosswalk.mjs, exited 0. A final related-to mapping from an RMF level-4 source into CSF yielded deterministic suggested=1/confidence=low; proposeCrosswalkAssessment returned an error. The tool exposed in AGENTS["crosswalk-analyst"] accepted current=4/confidence=high with an explicitly mapping-only rationale, stored only {nodeId,current}, produced canApprove=true/sources=[], and an exact reviewToken approval applied level 4. Result is persisted in provider-crosswalk-result.json. Counterevidence: this is not autonomous application—status initially remained pending, a person still approved, and generic warnings said no artifact/check was attached and readiness does not establish compliance. Those safeguards do not retain the required mapping basis or enforce projection confidence/caps.
findings.recommendation: Expose a provider crosswalk proposal tool whose input selects the target and whose implementation invokes the trusted recomputation helper; remove the general assessment write tool from Crosswalk Analyst or enforce at the service/run boundary that crosswalk-origin assessments carry the validated projection. Add a provider-tool dispatch regression using the same weak mapping and a strong mapping, without contacting a model; preserve general human-reviewed direct assessments for the assessor workflow.

limitations: This was a bounded source review plus one decision-critical synthetic reproduction, not the full milestone acceptance gate. Existing test cases were inspected but not executed; PostgreSQL, browser, full suites and real-provider behavior were not tested.
The reproduction invokes the exact tool exposed to the provider runtime with a synthetic tool call; it establishes an admitted behavior, not that a real model was observed to choose it.
Live data/network access and M4 exports were outside scope. Licensing review traced the touched corpus/proposal paths, not an exhaustive audit of every historical content source.

The lead concurrently edited unrelated diagnostics/lifecycle sections. Start/end file hashes and final relevant visua section hashes are recorded in claims-review-source.json; source changes after those pins require targeted revalidation.

After receiving the reproduced finding, the lead announced a narrow correction to provider crosswalk routing and service enforcement, including legacy preview/apply. That correction is pending separate verification and is not represented as fixed or tested by this review. The original reproduction and result remain unchanged.
